reason: The dome and lens both bend light, so combining them seems like a useful start on focusing the image.
expectation: I expect them to form part of the eye's focusing front, though the iris will still be needed to control light.

alternatives.reason: The light-sensitive cells and nerve fibres also make sense together, but I want to build the focusing front first.

effect: The dome and lens focus light toward the back; the iris is still needed to control how much enters.
reaction: The converging rays make their shared job clear.
reason: Adding the iris should complete the light-controlling part of the eye front.
expectation: I expect the iris to sit in front of the lens and adjust the opening that lets light through.

alternatives.reason: The light-sensitive lining is also a goal, but I want to finish the eye front first.

effect: The eye front is complete: the iris controls incoming light while the dome and lens focus it.
reaction: The picture makes the parts' different jobs clear.
reason: This is the only available combination, and it follows the goal to build a light-sensitive lining with an outgoing nerve.
expectation: I expect a lining that detects light and sends signals through nerve fibres, though I'm unsure how the cells connect.

effect: The light-sensitive cells and nerve cells form the retina, with their fibres gathered into the optic nerve. The next goal is to join the eye's front and lining.
reaction: The picture makes the new terms easier to connect to their jobs.
reason: This is the only available combination and directly follows the new goal.
expectation: I expect an eye cutaway with light focused onto the retina and signals leaving through the optic nerve.

effect: The completed eye shows how the focusing front and retina work together, with the optic nerve carrying information toward the brain.
reaction: Seeing the leaf's light focused on the retina tied the pieces together clearly.

mostWorthwhile.text: Joining the eye front and retina was most worthwhile because it brought the whole path from light to nerve signals together.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding the iris was clear but less engaging: its place and light-control job were already strongly hinted.

surprise.text: I learned that the light-sensitive lining is called the retina and that its nerve fibres gather into the optic nerve.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt particularly arbitrary. The picture descriptions and goals gave each pairing a purpose, though the last two combinations were the only available actions.

continue.text: I would probably continue: building the eye in two understandable parts and then seeing them work together made me curious about other organs.
